@@ -747,6 +747,7 @@ everything target-specific is independent.
 | D48 | Alternative delegate slot: `-> IDENT` / `-> IDENT(args...)` | **A rule alternative's trailing slot grows a sixth shape: `-> IDENT` delegates that alternative's action to a named implementation, instead of an inline `{% %}`/`{%? %}` action. `Alt` (Core AST) becomes a flat, epsilon-free six-alternative cross-product — `SymList Label Action \| SymList Label Delegate \| SymList Label \| SymList Action \| SymList Delegate \| SymList` — never a wrapper nonterminal with an empty alternative (same epsilon-free discipline as D27). A new reserved `ARROW` token (`"->"`) joins the Core's own lexis at the same level as `PLUS`/`STAR`/`LANGLE`/`RANGLE`/`COMMA`; confirmed zero collision risk empirically, since a bare `-`/`->` had no prior meaning anywhere in the notation's own vocabulary (an unquoted `-` was an "unexpected character" lex error before this). Extended in the same phase's direct follow-up with a parenthesized, comma-separated argument list — `Delegate : ARROW IDENT \| ARROW IDENT '(' ArgList ')'`, `ArgList : Arg \| ArgList ',' Arg` (left-recursive, matching the notation's own house style for comma lists, reusing the `COMMA` token already declared for macro-call `Args`), `Arg : IDENT \| TERM_LIT \| NUMBER` — enabling host commands like `-> channel(HIDDEN)`, `-> type(TOKEN_TYPE)`, or arbitrary custom ones like `-> my_custom(arg1, arg2, 42)`. A new reserved `NUMBER` token (`/[0-9]+/`) joins the lexis for the bare-number argument shape; the core `lr`-notation lexer had no numeric token class before this (not to be confused with `Tokens.scala`'s separate bespoke token-LINE parser, a different lexer). `Alt.delegate` changed from `Option[String]` to `Option[DelegateSpec]` (`case class DelegateSpec(name: String, args: Vector[String])`, `args` empty for the bare form) and `IRRule.delegate` from `Option[String]` to `Option[IRDelegate]` (mirroring exactly) — a breaking shape change to a field that had not shipped to any real-world consumer yet, so modifying rather than versioning it was judged acceptable. Each argument is carried through as its own literal source text (an identifier's name, a literal's unescaped content, or a number's digit string) — the IR never interprets it further. Mutually exclusive with an action by construction, not a runtime check (the grammar has no production combining both, so writing both is a parse error). Verified conflict-free under Canonical/LALR/IELR, including in `Gramaire.gram.md` (the full-notation meta-grammar), which already had its own `ARROW` token for `-> skip`/`-> pass` lexer-command modifiers and safely reuses it here since the two occur in disjoint rule contexts.** | Delegating an alternative's action to something named rather than inlined is the natural next step once actions exist as a slot at all (D3/D25) — a consumer application (or, in a later phase, a fenced implementation elsewhere in the same file) can supply the real implementation, without forcing every action into `{% %}` source text. Parameterization followed immediately once the bare form landed, since a real delegate target (a lexer channel, a token-type override, a custom host command) almost always needs at least one argument to be useful — deferring it would have meant re-deriving the same `Alt`/`IRRule` field-shape change a second time. Scoped narrowly this phase: only the syntax + IR field land; resolving the name (consumer-supplied lookup now, fenced-implementation lookup later) is explicitly deferred to the `## Externals` phase, which is a separate, later piece of work.
